cases.purpose: login become refuses every argument shape (plain, --auth-token, --auth-fd, unknown user) when the real uid is not 0, with status 1, the documented diagnostic and no change to credentials, environment or working directory.
cases.oracle: login.c bl_become_cmd step 1 ("Reject if real uid != 0") and the diagnostic "become: only root may drop privileges (uid=N)"; identity and environment before and after come from GNU id and the shell itself, the uid from GNU id -u.
cases.comparison: Exact stdout: per variant the exit status and whether the diagnostic names the real uid, then identity/cwd/environment unchanged flags; the refusal precedes user lookup, token handling and any exec.
cases.script:
export PHCLIB_PASSWD=$PWD/nonexistent-passwd canary=keep-me
uid=$(/usr/bin/id -u)
before=$(/usr/bin/id; echo "$PWD|$canary|$$")
run() {
  local label=$1; shift
  login become "$@" > out.txt 2> err.txt < /dev/null
  local rc=$?
  local err; err=$(< err.txt)
  local out; out=$(< out.txt)
  local named=no; [[ $err == *"login: become: only root may drop privileges (uid=$uid)"* ]] && named=yes
  echo "$label rc=$rc diagnostic=$named stdout-empty=$([[ -z $out ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
}
run plain alice
run command alice -c true
run auth-token alice --auth-token 00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff
run auth-fd alice --auth-fd 9
run unknown-user no-such-user
after=$(/usr/bin/id; echo "$PWD|$canary|$$")
[[ $before == "$after" ]] && echo "identity-cwd-environment=unchanged" || echo "identity-cwd-environment=CHANGED"
cases.stdout:
plain rc=1 diagnostic=yes stdout-empty=yes
command rc=1 diagnostic=yes stdout-empty=yes
auth-token rc=1 diagnostic=yes stdout-empty=yes
auth-fd rc=1 diagnostic=yes stdout-empty=yes
unknown-user rc=1 diagnostic=yes stdout-empty=yes
identity-cwd-environment=unchanged

cases.purpose: With input at EOF login prints /etc/issue followed by the exact "<hostname> login: " prompt on stdout, nothing on stderr, and fails with status 1.
cases.oracle: login.c bl_login_cmd: /etc/issue is copied verbatim, then the hostname from the first line of /etc/hostname (fallback bash-os) plus " login: " is flushed before the username read; the script reads both files itself with the read builtin.
cases.comparison: Exact bytes of the redirected stdout against issue-bytes plus hostname plus " login: ", exact empty stderr and status.
cases.script:
export BASHAUTH_LOGIN_POLICY=$PWD/policy.none BPW_LOCK_DIR=$PWD/lock BASHLOGIN_REQUIRE_KERNEL_TOKEN=0
hn=bash-os; [[ -r /etc/hostname ]] && IFS= read -r hn < /etc/hostname
issue=; [[ -r /etc/issue ]] && { IFS= read -r -d '' issue < /etc/issue; true; }
login --max-tries 1 < /dev/null > out.txt 2> err.txt
echo "rc=$?"
IFS= read -r -d '' got < out.txt || true
[[ $got == "${issue}${hn} login: " ]] && echo "prompt-bytes=exact" || echo "prompt-bytes=DIFFER"
[[ -s err.txt ]] && echo "stderr=nonempty" || echo "stderr=empty"
[[ -n $issue ]] && echo "issue=present" || echo "issue=absent"

Account rows are private PHCLIB_PASSWD/PHCLIB_SHADOW files whose Argon2id PHC hashes are generated by the guest argon2 CLI and cross-checked in setup against OpenSSL's independent ARGON2ID KDF. Expectations are fixed by the requirement text and POSIX PTY semantics, not copied from candidate output. Policy syntax is the documented 'account required securetty tty=...|file=/...' and 'account required time deny'; a correct password for uid 0 is required to reach the check, and a permitted login proceeds to the session-accounting stage, which an unprivileged caller cannot complete (open /var/run/utmp fails), so that diagnostic marks passing the gate.
cases.comparison: Eight login invocations with correct passwords; per invocation the first output line after the password is anchored (refusal text or the utmp-stage diagnostic) and the exit status 1 is read back.
cases.setup_script:
mkdir -p lock
phc_cli() { local h; h=$(printf '%s' "$1" | /usr/bin/argon2 somesalt -id -t 1 -k 1024 -p 1 -l 32 -r); printf '$argon2id$v=19$m=1024,t=1,p=1$736f6d6573616c74$%s' "$h"; }
phc_ssl() { local hx h; hx=$(printf '%s' "$1" | /usr/bin/od -An -v -tx1 | /usr/bin/tr -d ' \n'); h=$(/usr/bin/openssl kdf -keylen 32 -kdfopt "hexpass:$hx" -kdfopt hexsalt:736f6d6573616c74 -kdfopt iter:1 -kdfopt memcost:1024 -kdfopt lanes:1 -kdfopt threads:1 ARGON2ID | /usr/bin/tr -d ':\n' | /usr/bin/tr 'A-F' 'a-f'); printf '$argon2id$v=19$m=1024,t=1,p=1$736f6d6573616c74$%s' "$h"; }
[[ $(phc_cli oracle-check) == "$(phc_ssl oracle-check)" ]]

cat > passwd <<'P'
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash
alice:x:3001:3001:Alice:/home/alice:/bin/bash
P
{ printf 'root:%s:19000:0:99999:7:::\n' "$(phc_cli root-secret)"; printf 'alice:%s:19000:0:99999:7:::\n' "$(phc_cli alice-secret)"; } > shadow
printf '%s\n' 'account required securetty tty=tty1' > policy.sec1
printf 'tty2 # console\n#tty4\ntty3\n' > securetty
printf 'account required securetty file=%s/securetty\n' "$PWD" > policy.sec2
printf '%s\n' 'account required time deny' > policy.time
printf '%s\n' 'auth required lockout max=2 window=600 duration=120' > policy.lock
cases.script:
export PHCLIB_PASSWD=$PWD/passwd PHCLIB_SHADOW=$PWD/shadow BPW_LOCK_DIR=$PWD/lock BASHAUTH_LOGIN_POLICY=$PWD/policy.none BASHLOGIN_REQUIRE_KERNEL_TOKEN=0
BASHAUTH_LOGIN_POLICY=$PWD/policy.sec1 login --max-tries 1 -t tty9; echo "v1=refused-tty rc=$?"
BASHAUTH_LOGIN_POLICY=$PWD/policy.sec1 login --max-tries 1 -t tty1; echo "v2=listed-tty rc=$?"
BASHAUTH_LOGIN_POLICY=$PWD/policy.sec2 login --max-tries 1 -t tty3; echo "v3=file-tty rc=$?"
BASHAUTH_LOGIN_POLICY=$PWD/policy.sec2 login --max-tries 1 -t /dev/tty2; echo "v4=file-tty-dev-prefix-comment rc=$?"
BASHAUTH_LOGIN_POLICY=$PWD/policy.sec2 login --max-tries 1 -t tty4; echo "v5=file-commented-out rc=$?"
BASHAUTH_LOGIN_POLICY=$PWD/policy.sec1 login --max-tries 1 ; echo "v6=no-tty-name rc=$?"
BASHAUTH_LOGIN_POLICY=$PWD/policy.sec1 login --max-tries 1 -t tty9; echo "v7=nonroot-unrestricted rc=$?"
BASHAUTH_LOGIN_POLICY=$PWD/policy.time login --max-tries 1 -t tty1; echo "v8=time-deny rc=$?"

Password: \r\nRoot login refused on this tty\.\r\n
Password: \r\nRoot login refused on unknown tty\.\r\n
